CVE-2019-20354->CVE-2020-24572.label: conditional
CVE-2019-20354->CVE-2020-24572.evidence: CVE-2019-20354: 'download arbitrary files from the Raspberry Pi'; CVE-2020-24572: 'With authenticated access ... RaspAP'
CVE-2019-20354->CVE-2020-24572.reason: Credential theft would make B reachable, but the texts do not say the files contain RaspAP credentials or that RaspAP runs on the same Pi.

CVE-2019-20354->CVE-2021-38759.label: unsupported
CVE-2019-20354->CVE-2021-38759.evidence: CVE-2021-38759: 'has the raspberry default password for the pi account. If not changed, attackers can gain administrator privileges'
CVE-2019-20354->CVE-2021-38759.reason: B only needs the default password to be unchanged; A adds nothing to enabling it, and reading /etc/shadow is not stated.

CVE-2019-3562->CVE-2020-1885.label: conditional
CVE-2019-3562->CVE-2020-1885.evidence: CVE-2019-3562: 'potentially execute code' in Oculus Browser; CVE-2020-1885: 'local users ... in Oculus Desktop ... on Windows'
CVE-2019-3562->CVE-2020-1885.reason: Needs code execution to actually happen and to land as a local user on the same Windows host as Oculus Desktop; neither is stated.

CVE-2019-3562->CVE-2021-24038.label: conditional
CVE-2019-3562->CVE-2021-24038.evidence: same texts as above; CVE-2021-24038: 'expose a privileged process handle to an unprivileged process'
CVE-2019-3562->CVE-2021-24038.reason: Same unstated assumptions (code execution; same host).

CVE-2020-1885->CVE-2021-24038.label: unsupported
CVE-2020-1885->CVE-2021-24038.reason: B needs only unprivileged local access, which A already presupposes; the claimed mechanism (overwrite the launcher binary) is not in either text.

CVE-2020-24572->CVE-2021-38545.label: unsupported
CVE-2020-24572->CVE-2021-38545.evidence: CVE-2021-38545: 'remote attackers to recover speech signals from an LED ... via a telescope'
CVE-2020-24572->CVE-2021-38545.reason: Glowworm needs optical line of sight, not a foothold; the claimed signal-enhancement mechanism is not in the texts.

CVE-2020-24572->CVE-2021-38759.label: unsupported
CVE-2020-24572->CVE-2021-38759.evidence: CVE-2020-24572: 'execute commands on the system'; CVE-2021-38759: 'If not changed ...'
CVE-2020-24572->CVE-2021-38759.reason: A's postcondition (command execution, privilege unstated) does not establish B's precondition (default password unchanged).

CVE-2021-38545->CVE-2019-20354.label: unsupported
CVE-2021-38545->CVE-2019-20354.reason: Assumes credentials are spoken aloud; not in the texts.

CVE-2021-38545->CVE-2021-38759.label: unsupported
CVE-2021-38545->CVE-2021-38759.reason: Assumes the default password is spoken aloud; not in the texts.

CVE-2021-38759->CVE-2019-20354.label: conditional
CVE-2021-38759->CVE-2019-20354.evidence: CVE-2021-38759: 'gain administrator privileges'; CVE-2019-20354: 'from the Raspberry Pi'
CVE-2021-38759->CVE-2019-20354.reason: Admin on the Pi could expose piSignage credentials if piSignage runs on that Pi, but admin can read files directly, so A's file read is not what enables it; kept conditional under the favourable reading.

CVE-2021-38759->CVE-2020-24572.label: conditional
CVE-2021-38759->CVE-2020-24572.evidence: CVE-2021-38759: 'gain administrator privileges'; CVE-2020-24572: 'the underlying OS (Raspberry Pi) running this software'
CVE-2021-38759->CVE-2020-24572.reason: Admin on the OS could reach RaspAP's configuration if it runs there, but the texts do not say RaspAP shares the Pi account's credentials.
